oil.summary: Crude prices extended their brutal multi-week rout on Thursday, with WTI shedding another 3.48% to $74.10/bbl and Heating Oil leading losses at -4.81%. The proximate catalyst is the formal signing of the US-Iran ceasefire deal, which reopens the Strait of Hormuz and immediately unleashes pent-up supply: reports indicate more than 60 million barrels of Persian Gulf crude are queued for Asia-bound shipments. Iranian tankers have already reappeared, signalling a swift export restart. Meanwhile, G7 nations agreed to escalate sanctions on Russian crude revenues, and Trump's sanctions waiver on Russian oil expired today — adding complexity for key buyers such as India. Analysts warn that even with Russian sanctions tightening, the state of global inventories is sufficiently bearish to cap any recovery. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting, reflecting how deeply the market is now pricing in oversupply.
drivers: Hormuz reopening and Iranian tanker restart flood market with 60+ million barrels of deferred supply
US-Iran ceasefire deal formally signed, removing the geopolitical risk premium that had supported prices
G7 escalates Russian oil sanctions and Trump's waiver expires, but bearish inventory backdrop limits any offsetting price support

gas.summary: Natural gas markets delivered a stark divergence on Thursday. Henry Hub edged up 2.51% to $3.224/MMBtu, continuing a modest four-week grind higher, while European TTF plunged 2.82% to €40.735/MWh — now down over 21% in a month. The TTF weakness mirrors the crude complex, as Hormuz reopening eases broader energy supply anxiety and reduces LNG diversion premiums into Europe. G7 sanctions on Russian gas exports add a structural uncertainty to European supply, but this was insufficient to stem today's selling. On the demand side, India's energy import bill surged 82% in May driven by LNG and crude arrivals, though domestic fuel prices are likely to remain sticky according to the country's petroleum ministry. The gas-specific news flow is relatively thin beyond these macro cross-currents.
drivers: TTF drops sharply as Hormuz reopening deflates European energy supply risk premium
G7 sanctions on Russian gas exports introduce medium-term European supply uncertainty but provided no price floor today
Henry Hub diverges higher on domestic US dynamics; India LNG import surge highlights ongoing Asian demand strength

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs held essentially flat at $75.38 (-0.07%), showing unusual resilience against a backdrop of crashing energy input costs. Over the past month EUAs are up 6.48%, even as TTF has collapsed 21% — a decoupling worth watching. The power and carbon desk faces a mixed macro backdrop: UK PM Starmer pledged a £210 million nuclear energy package for Ukraine alongside fresh Russia sanctions at the G7, while the US-Iran deal's nuclear program ambiguities — including the unresolved fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile — keep geopolitical risk alive. Australia's renewable pipeline surged roughly 30% following government tenders for nearly 10 gigawatts of new capacity, a positive structural signal. A separate note flags an emerging power infrastructure deficit as a key risk to AI-sector growth forecasts, though detail on that piece is limited.
drivers: EUA prices resilient and up ~6.5% on the month despite collapsing gas costs, suggesting carbon market tightness is decoupled from energy input deflation
G7 nuclear energy support package for Ukraine and unresolved Iran nuclear stockpile question keep geopolitical uncertainty elevated in the power complex
Australia's renewable pipeline jumps ~30% post-government tenders; AI power demand infrastructure gap flagged as a latent systemic risk
